history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 389 / Raghunath Temple (same Rampur Bushahr temple). Stone temple dedicated to Ram (Raghunath, the Ram avatar of Vishnu), located on the main road of Rampur town opposite the Narsingh temple and now surrounded by a dharamshala. A stone-engraved idol of Hanuman sits outside the main temple and on its outer walls; the architecture follows the regional Nagara-influenced stone-and-wood style. It is described as one of the oldest temples in Rampur, the last capital of the Bushahr dynasty. IMPORTANT: not to be confused with the far better-known Raghunath temples of Kullu (built by Raja Jagat Singh, 17th c.) or Jammu (built by Gulab Singh, 19th c.) - no reliable founding date or builder is documented for the Rampur temple (verify). Coordinates are approximate (town main-road location; the temple stands on Rampur's main road, ~100 m from the geocoded point).

name: Raghunath Temple, Rampur Bushahr
town_description: Rampur (Rampur Bushahr) is a historic town in Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Sutlej River along the old Hindustan-Tibet Road. It was the last capital of the Bushahr dynasty and remains a trading centre famous for the Lavi fair (November) and Kinnauri shawls. It is ~132 km from Shimla via NH-5. The town has several old temples (Raghunath, Narsingh, Maheshwar) plus a Buddhist Dungyur temple inaugurated by the Dalai Lama in 2006.

travel.road: On NH-5 (old NH-22) Shimla-Kinnaur highway; regular HRTC buses from Shimla, Rampur and Kinnaur

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November; Lavi fair (November) is the cultural high point
